cos.text: Explain the principles of professional ethics, relevant laws, regulatory guidelines, and ethical responsibilities applicable to physiotherapy practice, research, education, and patient care.

Apply ethical principles, informed consent procedures, research ethics guidelines, and professional legal provisions to clinical decision-making, physiotherapy diagnosis, individualized care planning, research, and academic case scenarios.

Analyze professional ethical challenges, communication processes, conflicts of interest, publication ethics, and considerations for vulnerable populations in physiotherapy assessment, diagnosis, intervention, practice, and research.

Evaluate management and administrative principles, quality assurance strategies, communication practices, and organizational processes for safe, effective, patient-centred physiotherapy service delivery and individualized care.

Analyze educational philosophies, adult learning theories, learning processes, motivation, and teaching–learning methods relevant to physiotherapy education, clinical training, patient education, and community practice.

Design outcome-oriented teaching and learning activities by integrating educational principles, Bloom's Taxonomy, Miller's Pyramid, teaching methods, educational technology, and clinical competence frameworks to develop clinical reasoning, physiotherapy diagnosis, and individualized care-planning competencies.

pos.title: Communication

pos.title: Diagnosis and plan of care

pos.title: Evidence based practice

pos.title: Teaching and learning principles
pos.text: Apply learning and teaching principles in educational, clinical and community settings

pos.title: Team Member

pos.title: Ethical and legal standards

units.title: Ethics and Law in Physiotherapy
units.topics: LEM 1.1–1.10: Principles and evolution of ethics; Helsinki Declaration; Nuremberg Code; autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence and justice; professionalism; ethical principles in physiotherapy practice; privacy, confidentiality, shared decision-making and informed consent; ICMR guidelines; informed consent process; IEC roles and responsibilities; vulnerable populations; conflict of interest; publication ethics; ICMJE authorship and plagiarism; NCAHP Act, Consumer Protection Act, Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act; ethical issues in clinical practice, research and academics.

units.title: Management and Administration in Physiotherapy
units.topics: LEM 2.1–2.5: Principles and applications of management and administration; management process including planning, organizing, staffing, finance, marketing, controlling and directing; quality assurance and Total Quality Management; hospital quality assurance, medical audit and international quality systems; communication process, barriers and types of communication; written and oral communication; hospital as an organization; functions and types of hospitals; management and establishment of a physiotherapy service unit.

units.title: Management of Teaching Institution and Educational Methodology in Physiotherapy
units.topics: LEM 3.1–3.6: Aims and objectives of education; agencies and types of education; educational philosophies; taxonomy of educational objectives; physiotherapy education and NEP; adult learning theories, learning styles and motivation; teaching-learning process; factors and laws of learning; role of teacher; teaching skills and methods; classroom and clinical teaching; lesson and unit planning; teaching aids and educational technology; Intended Learning Outcomes; Tyler's principles; Bloom's Taxonomy; Miller's Pyramid; clinical competence; Dreyfus' Model; entrepreneurship in physiotherapy practice.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 1.1. Principles of Ethics: History and evolution of ethics; Helsinki Declaration; Nuremberg Code
lessonPlan.slo: Explain the historical development of research ethics and the significance of the Nuremberg Code and Helsinki Declaration in physiotherapy research and practice.
lessonPlan.resource: Helsinki Declaration; Nuremberg Code; LMS material

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 1.1. Principles of Ethics: Autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence and justice
lessonPlan.slo: Explain the four fundamental principles of ethics and relate them to physiotherapy practice and patient care.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 1.2. Professionalism
lessonPlan.slo: Explain the characteristics of professionalism and professional responsibilities in physiotherapy practice, education and research.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 1.3. Ethics in Professional Practice: Principles of practice; privacy; confidentiality; shared decision-making
lessonPlan.slo: Apply ethical principles of privacy, confidentiality and shared decision-making to physiotherapy clinical scenarios.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 1.3. Ethics in Professional Practice: Informed consent; equality, equity and justice
lessonPlan.slo: Apply informed consent, equality, equity and justice principles to individualized physiotherapy care and professional practice.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 1.4. ICMR Guidelines: General principles and responsible conduct of research

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 1.4. ICMR Guidelines: Risk-benefit assessment

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 1.5. Informed Consent Process: Components of informed consent document

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 1.5. Informed Consent Process: Procedure for obtaining informed consent; special situations
lessonPlan.slo: Apply appropriate procedures for obtaining informed consent in routine and special clinical/research situations.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 1.6. Roles and Responsibilities of IEC: Ethical review process and classification of projects

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 1.6. Roles and Responsibilities of IEC: Roles of IEC members; communication with investigators and authorities

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 1.7. Ethics in Special and Vulnerable Populations: Types of vulnerability and vulnerable populations

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 1.7. Ethics in Special and Vulnerable Populations: Challenges and guidelines

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 1.9. Publication Ethics: Importance of publishing; authorship according to ICMJE

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 1.10. Laws Governing Physiotherapy Practice: NCAHP Act

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 1.10. Laws Governing Physiotherapy Practice: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act
lessonPlan.slo: Analyze the rights, accessibility and equality considerations relevant to physiotherapy services for persons with disabilities.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 2.2. Management Process: Planning, organizing and staffing
lessonPlan.slo: Apply planning, organizing and staffing principles to the establishment and functioning of a physiotherapy service unit.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 2.2. Management Process: Finance, marketing, controlling and directing
lessonPlan.slo: Analyze basic financial, marketing, controlling and directing functions relevant to physiotherapy administration.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 2.3. Quality Assurance: Total Quality Management and basis of quality management
lessonPlan.slo: Explain principles of quality assurance and Total Quality Management relevant to physiotherapy services.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 2.3. Quality Assurance: Hospital quality assurance, medical audit and international quality systems
lessonPlan.slo: Evaluate quality assurance processes, medical audit and quality systems used in healthcare organizations.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 2.4. Communication: Process, barriers and types of communication
lessonPlan.slo: Analyze the communication process, barriers and types of communication relevant to physiotherapy practice and administration.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 2.4. Communication: Written vs. oral communication; elements of good communication
lessonPlan.slo: Demonstrate effective written and oral communication appropriate for patients, colleagues and healthcare organizations.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 2.5. Hospital as an Organization: Functions and types of hospitals
lessonPlan.slo: Explain the organizational structure, functions and types of hospitals and their relevance to physiotherapy services.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 2.5. Management in Hospital Setting: Setting up a physiotherapy service unit
lessonPlan.slo: Design a basic organizational and operational plan for establishing a physiotherapy service unit within a hospital.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 3.1. Education: Definition, aims and objectives; agencies of education; formal and informal education
lessonPlan.slo: Explain the meaning, aims, objectives and major forms and agencies of education relevant to physiotherapy.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 3.1. Education: Philosophies of education; taxonomy of educational objectives; essentials of physiotherapy education; NEP
lessonPlan.slo: Analyze major educational philosophies and relate educational objectives and NEP principles to physiotherapy education.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 3.2. Basics of Adult Learning Theories: Learning styles and motivation
lessonPlan.slo: Analyze adult learning theories, learning styles and motivational factors relevant to postgraduate physiotherapy education.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 3.3. Concept of Teaching-Learning: Nature, types and stages of learning; factors affecting learning
lessonPlan.slo: Analyze the teaching-learning process, stages of learning and factors influencing learning in physiotherapy students and clinical learners.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 3.3. Concept of Teaching-Learning: Laws of learning, learning styles, teaching-learning process and role of teacher
lessonPlan.slo: Analyze principles and laws of learning and relate the teacher's role to effective physiotherapy education and clinical training.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 3.4. Teaching Skills and Methods: Teaching skills and classroom teaching methods
lessonPlan.slo: Demonstrate selection of appropriate classroom teaching methods according to learner needs and intended outcomes.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 3.4. Teaching Skills and Methods: Clinical teaching methods
lessonPlan.slo: Select and apply appropriate clinical teaching methods for developing physiotherapy clinical competence.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 3.4. Planning of Teaching: Lesson planning, unit planning, teaching aids and educational technology
lessonPlan.slo: Design a structured lesson plan using appropriate teaching aids and educational technology for physiotherapy education.

lessonPlan.topic: LEM 3.5. Formulating Intended Learning Outcomes: Tyler's principles and Bloom's Taxonomy
lessonPlan.slo: Formulate measurable intended learning outcomes using Tyler's principles and appropriate levels of Bloom's Taxonomy.

evaluation.description: Written examination on Unit I (Ethics and Law) content taught up to the scheduled test, including principles/history of ethics, Helsinki Declaration, Nuremberg Code, professionalism, ethical practice, informed consent, IEC, vulnerable populations, and/or publication ethics as covered before the test.

Written examination on the Management & Administration and Educational Methodology content taught up to the scheduled test, including management principles/processes, quality/communication/hospital organization as applicable, education and adult learning, teaching-learning process, teaching methods and related educational methodology topics as covered before the test.

Course-wide application assignments: (1) ethical/COI/publication-ethics case analysis, (2) physiotherapy service-unit management/administration task, and (3) lesson plan/ILO/assessment-design task. Individual or group submission as decided by the course team.
